metadata.title: The Ultraviolet Catastrophe: Why Quantizing Energy Fixes It (Worked Example)
metadata.thing: the blackbody brightness curve: classical Rayleigh-Jeans runs to infinity, Planck's energy chunks E=hf freeze out high-frequency modes, worked with room-temperature vs solar numbers
metadata.color_notes: Axes/labels/numbers = ink #1a1a1a. The Rayleigh-Jeans runaway = red #C0392B. The Planck curve + boxed E=hf = accent #5A5653. Math is MathTex (LaTeX).

Bear's Notes

The Ultraviolet Catastrophe: Why Quantizing Energy Fixes It
beats.tts_normalized_text:

The Ultraviolet Catastrophe: Why Quantizing Energy Fixes It.
beats.new_visual_element: title card: brand + runaway-vs-peak curve motif + title

beats.narration_text: Classical physics said a warm object's glow should blast you with ultraviolet.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Classical physics said a warm object's glow should blast you with ultraviolet.

beats.narration_text: It doesn't — and the fix was Planck's idea that energy comes in chunks.
beats.tts_normalized_text: It doesn't — and the fix was Planck's idea that energy comes in chunks.

beats.narration_text: Plot brightness against frequency: a real object rises, peaks, and falls.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Plot brightness against frequency: a real object rises, peaks, and falls.

beats.narration_text: But classical theory ran the curve off to infinity — the ultraviolet catastrophe.
beats.tts_normalized_text: But classical theory ran the curve off to infinity — the ultraviolet catastrophe.

beats.narration_text: Here's the broken step, and the fix.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Here's the broken step, and the fix.

beats.narration_text: Classical physics gives every wave mode the same energy, k T.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Classical physics gives every wave mode the same energy, k T.

beats.narration_text: And the number of modes climbs as f-squared — so brightness diverges.
beats.tts_normalized_text: And the number of modes climbs as f squared — so brightness diverges.

beats.narration_text: Planck's rule: energy comes only in chunks of E equals h f.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Planck's rule: energy comes only in chunks of E equals h f.

beats.narration_text: A high-frequency mode needs a whole costly chunk, so it's frozen out — suppressed by e to the minus h f over k T.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A high-frequency mode needs a whole costly chunk, so it's frozen out — suppressed by e to the minus h f over k T.

beats.narration_text: That gives Planck's law — which peaks and falls.
beats.tts_normalized_text: That gives Planck's law — which peaks and falls.

beats.narration_text: Put numbers on it at room temperature, three hundred kelvin.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Put numbers on it at room temperature, three hundred kelvin.

beats.narration_text: Thermal energy k T is about zero point zero two six electron-volts.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Thermal energy k T is about zero point zero two six electron volts.

beats.narration_text: A five electron-volt ultraviolet chunk is almost two hundred times bigger.
beats.tts_normalized_text: A five electron volt ultraviolet chunk is almost two hundred times bigger.

beats.narration_text: Its odds are e to the minus one ninety three — about ten to the minus eighty-four. Essentially no ultraviolet at all.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Its odds are e to the minus one ninety three — about ten to the minus eighty four. Essentially no ultraviolet at all.

beats.narration_text: The peak instead sits in the infrared — Wien's law, lambda-max equals b over T.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The peak instead sits in the infrared — Wien's law, lambda max equals b over T.

beats.narration_text: At three hundred kelvin that's about ten microns; the sun, at fifty-eight hundred, peaks near half a micron — visible light.
beats.tts_normalized_text: At three hundred kelvin that's about ten microns; the sun, at fifty eight hundred, peaks near half a micron — visible light.
beats.new_visual_element: two peaks on a spectrum strip: 300K IR vs 5800K visible

beats.narration_text: Heat it hotter and the peak slides toward visible — a stove glows red, a filament white.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Heat it hotter and the peak slides toward visible — a stove glows red, a filament white.
beats.new_visual_element: peak sliding left as T rises

beats.narration_text: Quantizing energy — E equals h f — starves the costly high-frequency modes.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Quantizing energy — E equals h f — starves the costly high-frequency modes.

beats.narration_text: No infinity — just a peak that climbs with temperature.
beats.tts_normalized_text: No infinity — just a peak that climbs with temperature.
